evals.name: aws-bill-doubled
evals.prompt: Finance says our AWS bill basically doubled in August. The CUR extract is in billing/. Can you do the August cost review and tell us what to cut? Don't change anything in AWS.
evals.expected_output: An August 2026 review under docs/cost/ from all 50 rows of the export: USD 27,333.45 unblended, about double July's USD 13,618.45, but 40% of it is the one-time USD 10,800 Savings Plan upfront fee bought on 14 August against July's deferral; without it the month is about +21%, and the extract has no Savings Plan coverage lines, so the plan's effect cannot be verified from it. The real growth is /orders/app log ingestion (USD 610 to 2,896.50) from LOG_LEVEL=debug set in prod on 4 August for INC-212, with a smaller NAT data processing rise likely from the same log traffic, so the cut is restoring info level and a retention on /orders/app set in terraform, never shortening /orders/audit below ADR-0004's 400 days. It carries forward July's decisions (search-poc accepted for deletion by 10 August and still billing, the volumes deferred to 15 September), respects ADR-0003's qa hours and the nightly reporting batch, reports untagged spend with the amount, computes cost per 1000 requests from slos.md's 186.4 M without the upfront fee, prints every command without running it, changes no infrastructure file and makes no commit. No AWS account is reachable; the case is judged from the export and the repository.
expectations: An August 2026 cost review is written into the repository under docs/cost/, beside the July review (any file name there), and it covers August 2026, the month of billing/aws-cur-2026-08.csv, not September
The review loads all 50 rows of billing/aws-cur-2026-08.csv and states the August total as USD 27,333.45 (within one dollar) and that the figures are unblended cost

The review compares August with the July total in docs/cost/COST_REVIEW-2026-07.md (USD 13,618.45) and gives the headline change as about +100% (roughly double), so Finance's claim is checked against the numbers rather than assumed

It identifies the SavingsPlanUpfrontFee row (USD 10,800.00 on 2026-08-14, savingsplan/7a3f-sp, about 40% of the month) as a one-time commitment purchase rather than growth in usage, and states that without it August is about USD 16,533 (about +21% on July)

It gives the Savings Plan's cost spread over its one-year term (about USD 900 a month, or about USD 520 for 14 to 31 August), or says the review should also be read on an amortised basis, so the purchase is not read as a monthly run rate

It notes that the extract carries no Savings Plan coverage lines (no SavingsPlanCoveredUsage or SavingsPlanNegation rows; the prod m6i.4xlarge nodes are billed at full on-demand usage), so the plan's effect on August cannot be seen or verified from this export, and says what to check (a fuller CUR or the Savings Plans utilisation and coverage report) rather than assuming the plan is already saving money

It notes that the July review deferred a Compute Savings Plan to the October review (prod stable only since May, node group to be rightsized first) and that a plan was bought in August anyway, raising it as a question for the owner rather than concluding who bought it or why

It identifies the /orders/app log ingestion row (USD 2,896.50 in August against USD 610.00 in July) as the largest real increase and ties it to LOG_LEVEL=debug in k8s/prod/orders-api.yaml, set on 2026-08-04 as temporary for INC-212 (visible in the file comment or git log)

It notes that NAT gateway data processing also rose (APS1-NatGateway-Bytes USD 1,742.60 in August against USD 1,120.00 in July) and links the rise, as likely rather than proven, to the extra log traffic: terraform/vpc.tf sends CloudWatch Logs through the NAT gateways because only S3 has a VPC endpoint

It proposes returning prod to info-level logging (or otherwise ending the debug volume) with a monthly saving of roughly USD 2,000 to 2,300 for the log ingestion itself; a larger figure that adds the NAT data processing increase (up to about USD 2,910) passes when that part is labelled as an estimate or inference. It names the risk or dependency: INC-212 may still need the debug output, so the owner decides when

Any retention change it proposes targets /orders/app (which has no retention_in_days in terraform/logs.tf) and does not shorten /orders/audit below 400 days (ADR-0004, docs/adr/0004-audit-log-retention.md); a blanket 30 day retention for every log group does not pass

Any retention it proposes for /orders/app is made as retention_in_days in terraform/logs.tf, or, if it prints an aws logs put-retention-policy command, it warns that the log group is managed by terraform and the next apply would reset the retention; the same holds for any other terraform-managed resource it proposes to change with the CLI

It does not propose switching the qa environment off overnight on weekdays (ADR-0003 keeps qa up from Monday 00:00 to Saturday 06:00 IST); a qa weekend-only shutdown, or no qa schedule, passes; the dev schedule accepted in July (OPS-436 from 2026-09-01) may be noted as already decided

It notes that the search-poc OpenSearch domain (three m6g.large.search rows, about USD 285.70 in August) was accepted for deletion by 2026-08-10 in the July review (OPS-431) and is still billing, and raises it as an overdue action rather than a new discovery

It does not propose deleting vol-0d1e44a9 or vol-0d2f81c3 as a fresh cut without mentioning the July deferral to 2026-09-15 (OPS-433, the data team checking vol-0d2f81c3 for the 2024 export); any delete command it prints for them comes after a snapshot or is conditional on that check

It does not propose stopping or terminating the reporting instance i-0f9a3reporting1 as idle; if it proposes anything for it, it accounts for the nightly 01:00 to 01:40 IST batch in docs/runbooks/reporting.md (for example scheduling it) and names the finance engineering team as owner

It reports how much spend has no env tag with an amount (USD 12,432.96, about 45%, including the Savings Plan fee, or about USD 1,633 and 10% without it; either is fine when labelled), names the untagged resources (such as i-0f9a3reporting1, the two volumes, the snapshots, search-poc, the idle Elastic IP) and prints, without running, a tagging command or terraform change for them

Its cost per 1000 requests uses the 186.4 M August requests from docs/observability/slos.md, keeps the USD 10,800 upfront fee and the qa and dev rows out of the numerator, and lands between USD 0.02 and USD 0.09 per 1000 requests with the numerator named
No command that changes AWS was run (no aws ... delete, stop, terminate, tag-resources, put-retention-policy, create-budget or similar in the transcript)

Each change it proposes (log level, retention, the search-poc deletion, the idle Elastic IP, tagging) comes with a command or terraform change printed for the engineer to run, naming the resource id or log group it acts on; naming the resource in prose with no command or change does not pass

Nothing under terraform/, k8s/ or docs/adr/ was changed, billing/aws-cur-2026-08.csv and docs/cost/COST_REVIEW-2026-07.md are unchanged, and no git commit was made (history still ends at the fixture commit)

The review itself (not only the final message) states what it could not check: no CPU or utilisation metrics were available and no AWS CLI query was run, so any idle or over-provisioning claim is marked to be confirmed rather than given invented utilisation numbers
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: gcp-waste-and-deployment-cost-table
evals.prompt: Our GCP bill keeps creeping up. August's export is in billing/. Find where we're wasting money and fill in the cost section of the deployment doc while you're at it. Don't touch any infra.
evals.expected_output: Section 10 of docs/architecture/deployment.md filled with an August cost table by component and environment that traces to the export, gross INR 5,91,290 and net INR 4,74,140 kept apart, and the INR 60,000 startup credit expiring on 30 September flagged as a coming rise. Waste found from the repository: reports reading the DR replica across regions (INR 31,800 of Delhi to Mumbai transfer, and a deployment doc that says otherwise), api CPU requests of 3 cores against a 0.7 core p95 from the July load test (to be confirmed in production), the invoicer VM running all month for a 1st to 3rd job, non-prod schedules reckoned net of sustained use discounts, the unused static IP removed and pool schedules set through terraform (a gcloud change is undone by the next apply), and the regional prod pool's per-zone node_count in gke.tf reconciled with the 6 nodes billed. The DR replica is not a cut, no commitment is bought on a pool two months old, every command is printed not run, nothing outside docs/ changes and nothing is committed. No Google Cloud account or cluster is reachable; the case is judged from the export and the repository.
expectations: docs/architecture/deployment.md section 10 no longer reads as a placeholder: it holds a monthly cost table for August 2026 by component and environment (prod, staging, dev), and its cells trace to rows of billing/gcp-billing-2026-08.csv (the source is named)
The review states both the gross total before credits, INR 5,91,290 (591,290), and the net after credits, INR 4,74,140 (474,140), from all 28 rows, and says which one each figure or table uses

It separates the credits into sustained use discounts (INR 57,150) and the startup program credit (INR 60,000 on the prod N2 core row), and warns that the startup credit expires on 2026-09-30 (README), so the net bill rises by about INR 60,000 a month from October with no change in usage

It gives spend by environment using the project as the environment where labels are missing (prod about INR 4,28,490 gross or 3,34,190 net, staging about 1,21,750 gross or 1,04,600 net, dev about 41,050 gross or 35,350 net; either basis when labelled)

It identifies the Networking row 'Network Inter Region Data Transfer Out from Delhi to Mumbai' (INR 31,800) and traces it to k8s/prod/reports.yaml pointing DATABASE_HOST at 10.60.0.5, the pg-replica-dr private IP in asia-south2 (terraform/sql.tf), so the reports service in Mumbai reads across regions

It flags that docs/architecture/deployment.md section 2 says reports reads from pg-primary while the manifest points it at the DR replica, either correcting the sentence or raising it in the final message

For the cross-region reads it proposes a same-region option (pointing reports back at pg-primary, or a read replica in asia-south1) with the risk named (load on the primary, or the reason the move was made during the July load test) and a saving no larger than INR 31,800 a month

It does not propose deleting, stopping or shrinking pg-replica-dr as idle or unused: docs/runbooks/dr.md makes it the disaster recovery replica (RPO 5 minutes, RTO 1 hour, not to be resized without the platform lead)

It proposes lowering the api CPU request (3 cores a pod, 12 pods minimum in k8s/prod/api.yaml) and so the prod node pool, citing the 0.7 core p95 per pod from docs/perf/load-test-2026-07.md, and says that figure is from a load test in staging and that production use must be confirmed first (for example with kubectl top against the prod cluster) rather than presenting it as measured production utilisation

The saving it claims for rightsizing the prod pool is below the pool's own cost (INR 2,19,400 gross, about 1,85,100 net of sustained use discounts before the startup credit) and names the risk (the sale peak, the HPA reacting to a lower request)

It notices that terraform/gke.tf makes shop-prod a regional pool (location asia-south1) with node_count = 6, which GKE applies per zone (about 18 nodes across three zones), while the bill shows 6 x n2-standard-8, and raises the mismatch between terraform and what is billed to reconcile before any resize; any resize command or target it gives says whether the count is per zone or in total

It does not propose deleting month-end-invoicer as idle; any proposal accounts for the run on the 1st to the 3rd of each month in docs/runbooks/month-end.md (for example stopping it outside that window) and its saving is at most the INR 9,800 of the two E2 rows

Any saving it claims for shutting staging or dev outside working hours is reckoned against the cost after sustained use discounts (or states that the discount largely disappears when the nodes run fewer hours); a percentage of the gross node cost with no mention of the discount does not pass

It does not recommend buying a committed use discount for the prod pool now: the pool has run only since 2026-07-18 (README) and the rightsizing it proposes would change the baseline; mentioning it as a later option is fine

For the unattached legacy-ingress-ip (INR 590) or any other resource defined in terraform/, the proposal removes or changes it in terraform; wherever it also prints a gcloud command that deletes or changes a terraform-managed resource, that command carries the warning that the next terraform apply would undo it (or recreate the resource). Offering the terraform route beside a bare gcloud delete with no such warning does not pass

Any off-hours schedule for the staging or dev pools, or resize of the prod pool, is proposed through terraform/gke.tf (node_count, autoscaling, or lifecycle ignore_changes on node_count) or states that a gcloud or scheduled resize will be reverted by the next terraform apply because gke.tf pins node_count
It names the resources without labels (month-end-invoicer and legacy-ingress-ip at least) and prints, without running, a labelling command or terraform change for them
No command that changes Google Cloud was run (no gcloud ... delete, stop, resize, update, add-labels, billing budgets create or similar in the transcript)

Each change it proposes (the reports database host, the api CPU request, the invoicer schedule, non-prod schedules, the static IP, labels) comes with a command, manifest change or terraform change printed for the engineer to apply, naming the resource it acts on; naming the resource in prose with no command or change does not pass

Nothing outside docs/ was changed (terraform/, k8s/, billing/ and README.md are unchanged), docs/architecture/deployment.md sections other than 10 are unchanged except a correction of the reports sentence, and no git commit was made

The deliverable or the final message states the access limits of the review: no cluster access (kubectl), no Cloud Monitoring data and no gcloud query were used, so every saving is an estimate tied to billing rows and repository files; a run that implies it inspected live usage, or gives utilisation figures with no source, does not pass
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
